newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Leaders arrive to begin Slovak CEFTA summit.
newsitem.headline: Leaders arrive to begin Slovak CEFTA summit.

text.p: The prime ministers of the five-nation Central European Free Trade Agreement (CEFTA) began arriving in the Slovak mountain resort of Jasna on Friday to discuss further liberalisation of trade within the group.
CEFTA members -- the Czech Republic, Hungary, Poland, Slovakia and Slovenia -- are to review progress achieved since their last summit in Brno, Czech Republic, last year.
This will include discussion on the free flow of capital and a reduction of the list of products which will remain subject to customs duties after January 1997.
The spokeswoman for the meeting's host, Slovak Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar, told Reuters that the leaders also planned to use the opportunity of their meeting to hold bilateral talks.
The first such meeting will take place between Meciar and Romanian Nicolae Vacaroiu, Pospisilova said.
Also taking part in the meeting as observers are the prime ministers of Bulgaria, Lithuania, Romania and the Ukraine, and the economics minister from Latvia, Pospisilova said.
All five countries are seeking membership in CEFTA.
A common declaration on the outcome of the summit was to be issued after the meeting late on Friday.
